summary_paragraph: A male patient with alcoholic and HCV-related cirrhosis, portal hypertension, and a history of bladder cancer with ileal conduit was admitted for bright red blood per rectum and alcohol intoxication. He reported multiple episodes of significant rectal bleeding, chronic abdominal pain, and dizziness. His hemoglobin remained stable at 7.6 g/dL after one unit of packed red blood cells. Abdominal ultrasound confirmed a patent TIPS without significant changes. He showed signs of possible hepatic encephalopathy, prompting an increase in lactulose frequency. His pain was poorly controlled on oxycodone, leading to a switch to Dilaudid as needed. He had acute kidney injury on top of chronic kidney disease, with creatinine stable at 1.4 mg/dL. Despite medical advice, he chose to leave against medical advice after two days, with instructions to continue lactulose, follow up with specialists, and return if symptoms worsened.
